info.title: Desktop Application Validation - Computer Use Agent Skill
info.description: Instructions for a computer use agent to launch and validate multiple Windows desktop applications via the Start Menu, confirming each opens and is functional.

post.summary: Open the Windows Start Menu and search for an application

steps: Click the Windows Start button (bottom-left of taskbar) OR press the Windows key
Wait for the Start Menu to open
Type the application name to search — Windows Search is instant, no need to click a search box first
Click the top result that matches the application name
Wait 3-5 seconds for the application to launch
Take a screenshot to confirm the application opened
tips: If the Start Menu closes unexpectedly, click the Start button again
If the wrong app appears in search results, refine the search term
Some apps may take longer to launch — wait up to 10 seconds before declaring failure
If nothing happens after clicking, try double-clicking the result
x-agent-instructions.verification: Take a screenshot after launch. Confirm the application window is visible and not showing an error dialog.

steps: Press the Windows key to open Start Menu
Type 'firefox'
Click 'Firefox' or 'Mozilla Firefox' in the search results
Wait for Firefox to open — may take 5-10 seconds on first launch
If a 'Set as default browser' dialog appears, click 'Not now' or 'Skip'
Wait for the browser home page or new tab page to load
Take a screenshot to confirm Firefox is open

success: Firefox window visible with address bar at the top
Home page, new tab page, or blank page loaded

commonDialogs.defaultBrowserPrompt: Click 'Not now' or 'Skip' — this is cosmetic, not a failure
commonDialogs.importDataPrompt: Click 'Cancel' or 'Skip' — not needed for validation
commonDialogs.updateAvailable: Click 'Later' or dismiss — not needed for validation
commonDialogs.restoreSession: Click 'Start New Session' to proceed cleanly

additionalValidation: Click the address bar
Type 'about:blank' and press Enter
Confirm the page loads (blank page is a valid response)
tips: Firefox may prompt to import bookmarks or set as default — dismiss all such dialogs
If Firefox opens in safe mode, close it and reopen normally
x-agent-instructions.verification: Screenshot showing Firefox window with visible address bar. Confirm no crash dialogs.

steps: Press the Windows key to open Start Menu
Type 'notepad++'
Click 'Notepad++' in the search results
Wait for Notepad++ to open — usually very fast (1-3 seconds)
If an update dialog appears, click 'Cancel' or 'No'
Take a screenshot to confirm Notepad++ is open

success: Notepad++ window visible with title bar showing 'Notepad++'
Menu bar visible (File, Edit, Search, View, Encoding, Language, etc.)
Tab bar visible at the top of the editing area
failure: Error dialog about missing DLL or runtime
Window appears but is completely unresponsive

additionalValidation: Click inside the text editing area
Type a few characters (e.g., 'test')
Confirm characters appear in the editor
Press Ctrl+Z to undo the typed text

commonDialogs.sessionRestore: Click 'OK' to restore previous session or 'Cancel' to start fresh — both are fine

tips: Notepad++ launches quickly — if it takes more than 5 seconds, something may be wrong
The update notification on startup is normal behavior
x-agent-instructions.verification: Screenshot showing Notepad++ with visible menu bar and editing area.

steps: Press the Windows key to open Start Menu
Type 'openoffice calc' or 'calc'
Click 'OpenOffice Calc' in the search results
Alternatively, search for 'scalc' if a direct shortcut exists
Wait for OpenOffice Calc to open — may take 5-10 seconds on first launch
If a 'Welcome' or 'Registration' dialog appears, click 'Close' or 'Skip'
Take a screenshot to confirm OpenOffice Calc is open

success: Menu bar visible (File, Edit, View, Insert, Format, etc.)
Sheet tabs visible at the bottom
failure: Error about missing Java runtime (may prevent some features but app still works)
Document recovery dialog loops without resolving

additionalValidation: Click on cell A1
Type a number (e.g., '123')
Press Enter
Click on cell B1
Type '=A1*2' and press Enter
Confirm cell B1 shows '246'
Press Ctrl+Z twice to undo

commonDialogs.documentRecovery: If file recovery dialog appears, click 'Discard' or 'Cancel'
commonDialogs.javaRequired: Click 'OK' to acknowledge — this is a warning, not a failure

tips: OpenOffice apps share a startup process — the first one to launch may be slower
If 'scalc' is listed as a program shortcut, use that directly
x-agent-instructions.verification: Screenshot showing OpenOffice Calc spreadsheet grid with formula bar visible.

steps: Press the Windows key to open Start Menu
Type 'openoffice draw' or 'draw'
Click 'OpenOffice Draw' in the search results
Alternatively, search for 'sdraw' if a direct shortcut exists
Wait for OpenOffice Draw to open
Take a screenshot to confirm OpenOffice Draw is open

success: Menu bar visible (File, Edit, View, Insert, Format, etc.)
Drawing toolbars visible on the left or bottom
Page panel visible on the side

additionalValidation: Click on the drawing canvas area
Confirm the canvas is clickable and the cursor changes appropriately
tips: OpenOffice Draw is the vector drawing component — it should show a blank page canvas
If 'sdraw' is listed as a program shortcut, use that directly
x-agent-instructions.verification: Screenshot showing OpenOffice Draw with visible canvas and drawing tools.

steps: Press the Windows key to open Start Menu
Type 'openoffice impress' or 'impress'
Click 'OpenOffice Impress' in the search results
Alternatively, search for 'simpress' if a direct shortcut exists
Wait for OpenOffice Impress to open — it may show a template/wizard dialog
If a template or presentation wizard dialog appears, click 'Blank Presentation' and then 'OK' or 'Create'
Take a screenshot to confirm OpenOffice Impress is open

success: Slide editing area visible in center
Slide panel visible on the left
Properties/formatting panel visible on the right (optional)

additionalValidation: Click on the main slide editing area
Confirm the slide canvas is interactive

commonDialogs.presentationWizard: Click through to 'Create' a blank presentation

tips: Impress may show a template chooser — this is normal startup behavior
If 'simpress' is listed as a program shortcut, use that directly
x-agent-instructions.verification: Screenshot showing OpenOffice Impress with slide editing area visible.

steps: Press the Windows key to open Start Menu
Type 'openoffice math' or 'math'
Click 'OpenOffice Math' in the search results
Alternatively, search for 'smath' if a direct shortcut exists
Wait for OpenOffice Math to open
Take a screenshot to confirm OpenOffice Math is open

success: Elements panel may be visible on the left or right
failure: Window appears but formula area is not shown

additionalValidation: Click in the formula input area (bottom pane)
Type a simple formula: 'a + b = c'
Confirm it renders in the preview area above
tips: OpenOffice Math is for creating mathematical formulas — it has a unique two-pane interface
If 'smath' is listed as a program shortcut, use that directly
The app may be less commonly known — if search returns no results, try 'openoffice math'
x-agent-instructions.verification: Screenshot showing OpenOffice Math with formula rendering area and input area visible.

steps: Press the Windows key to open Start Menu
Type 'openoffice'
Click 'OpenOffice' or 'OpenOffice Start Center' in the search results
Alternatively, search for 'soffice' if a direct shortcut exists
Wait for the OpenOffice Start Center to open
Take a screenshot to confirm the Start Center is open

success: List of recent documents visible (or empty state message)
Buttons/icons for creating new documents visible (Writer, Calc, Impress, Draw, Math, Base)
failure: Only a blank window with no UI

tips: The OpenOffice Start Center is the hub application that links to all OpenOffice components
If 'soffice' is a direct shortcut, it may launch this Start Center
Recent documents showing is normal — the app is working correctly
x-agent-instructions.verification: Screenshot showing OpenOffice Start Center with document type icons or recent files visible.

post.summary: Launch OpenOffice Writer Web (sweb) or Web component

steps: Press the Windows key to open Start Menu
Type 'sweb' or 'openoffice web'
Click the matching result in search
If no direct result, try searching for the full shortcut name
Wait for the application to open
Take a screenshot to confirm the application is open

success: Some form of editing or viewing area visible
failure: No matching application found in search

tips: 'sweb' may refer to OpenOffice Writer in web/HTML editing mode
It may also be a custom application or shortcut on this system
If the search returns no result, document this as 'not found' in the report
Try alternate search terms: 'web', 'openoffice writer web', 'sweb'
x-agent-instructions.verification: Screenshot showing whatever application opened, or screenshot of failed search results to document the state.

steps: Press the Windows key to open Start Menu
Type 'openoffice writer' or 'writer'
Click 'OpenOffice Writer' in the search results
Alternatively, search for 'swriter' if a direct shortcut exists
Wait for OpenOffice Writer to open
If a document recovery dialog appears, click 'Discard' or 'Cancel'
Take a screenshot to confirm OpenOffice Writer is open

success: Menu bar visible (File, Edit, View, Insert, Format, Styles, etc.)
Status bar visible at the bottom

additionalValidation: Click in the document editing area
Type a few words (e.g., 'Hello World')
Confirm text appears in the document
Press Ctrl+Z to undo

commonDialogs.documentRecovery: Click 'Discard' to start fresh — this is not a failure

tips: OpenOffice Writer is the most commonly used component — it should launch reliably
If 'swriter' is listed as a program shortcut, use that directly
x-agent-instructions.verification: Screenshot showing OpenOffice Writer with document area and toolbar visible.

post.summary: Perform basic validation steps for any open application

steps: Confirm the window title is visible and contains an expected application name
Confirm the main menu bar or toolbar is visible and not greyed out
Confirm there are no blocking error dialogs
Perform at least one interactive action (click, type, or navigate a menu)
Confirm the application responds to the interaction
Take a screenshot to record the validated state
passCriteria: UI elements are visible and not blocked by errors
Application responds to at least one user interaction
No crash dialogs or fatal error messages
failCriteria: Application shows a crash reporter or fatal error dialog
Application is completely unresponsive (frozen) for more than 15 seconds
tips: Minor warnings or non-blocking dialogs do NOT constitute failure
Slow startup is not a failure — allow adequate time
Record both pass and fail states clearly in the validation report

post.summary: Close the current application before launching the next

steps: Press Alt+F4 to close the active application window
If a 'Save changes?' dialog appears, click 'Don't Save' or 'Discard'
If Alt+F4 does not work, click the X button in the top-right corner of the window
Wait for the application to close fully before launching the next one
Take a screenshot to confirm the desktop is clear before proceeding
tips: Always close the previous application before launching the next to avoid resource conflicts
If an application is frozen, use Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) to force-close it
After closing OpenOffice apps, wait 2-3 seconds for background processes to terminate

steps: After testing all applications, compile the results into a structured report
For each application, record: Name, Status (PASS/FAIL/NOT FOUND), Notes
Include any error messages observed
Include the count of passed vs failed applications
Present the report in a clear table or list format

applicationOverview.name: Desktop Application Validator
applicationOverview.purpose: Launch each of the following applications via the Windows Start Menu and confirm they open and are functional: Firefox, Notepad++, OpenOffice Calc (scalc), OpenOffice Draw (sdraw), OpenOffice Impress (simpress), OpenOffice Math (smath), OpenOffice Start Center (soffice), OpenOffice Web (sweb), OpenOffice Writer (swriter)

windowLayout.desktop: Standard Windows desktop with taskbar at the bottom
windowLayout.startMenu: Accessed via Windows key or clicking the Start button (bottom-left)
windowLayout.searchBar: Typing immediately after pressing Windows key triggers search
windowLayout.taskbar: Running applications appear as icons in the taskbar — useful for switching between apps

coordinatePlanning.description: Applications are launched via Start Menu search — exact pixel coordinates are less critical than for canvas-based apps. Focus on clicking visible search results and UI elements.
coordinatePlanning.startButtonLocation: Bottom-left corner of the screen, approximately (30, 1060) on 1080p displays
coordinatePlanning.searchResults: Appear in the center of the Start Menu overlay — click the topmost relevant result
coordinatePlanning.closeButton: X button in the top-right corner of each window, approximately (rightEdge - 15, 15)

actionBatching.coreRule: For each application: search → launch → validate → close. Take a screenshot after launch and after validation. Close before moving to the next app.
screenshotTiming: After each application launches (to verify it opened)
After performing a basic interaction (to confirm responsiveness)
After observing any error or unexpected state
actionBatching.avoidUnnecessaryScreenshots: Do not screenshot between typing in search and clicking results — these are reliable actions

interactionPatterns.startMenuSearch: Press Windows key → type app name → click result
interactionPatterns.dismissDialogs: Press Escape or click Cancel/Skip/No buttons to dismiss non-essential dialogs
interactionPatterns.basicInteraction: Click on the main editing area and type a small amount of text to verify responsiveness

appNotInSearch.description: Application not found when searching by primary name
appNotInSearch.recovery: Try alternative search terms. Document as 'NOT FOUND' if all attempts fail.

startMenuNotOpening.description: Start Menu does not open when pressing Windows key
startMenuNotOpening.recovery: Click the Start button directly in the bottom-left corner of the taskbar

appFrozenOnLaunch.description: Application window appears but is unresponsive
appFrozenOnLaunch.recovery: Wait 15 seconds. If still frozen, open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc), find the process, and click 'End Task'. Mark as FAIL.

unexpectedDialog.description: A blocking dialog appears during validation
unexpectedDialog.recovery: Press Escape first. If dialog persists, read its content and click the most appropriate dismissal button (Cancel, No, Skip, Close).

openOfficeRecoveryDialog.description: OpenOffice asks to recover a previous session
openOfficeRecoveryDialog.recovery: Click 'Discard' — this is normal and not a failure

previousAppStillVisible.description: Previous application did not close fully
previousAppStillVisible.recovery: Click the X to close it, or use Alt+F4. Ensure the window is gone before launching the next app.

saveDialog.description: Save dialog appears when closing an app where test input was typed
saveDialog.recovery: Click 'Don't Save' or 'Discard Changes' to close without saving

validationStandards.passDefinition: Application window opens, main UI is visible, no fatal error dialogs, and the application responds to at least one user interaction.
validationStandards.failDefinition: Application does not open, shows a crash/fatal error dialog, or is completely unresponsive for more than 15 seconds.
validationStandards.notFoundDefinition: No matching application found in Start Menu after trying all reasonable search terms.
validationStandards.warningsAreOk: Non-blocking warnings, update prompts, registration dialogs, and default setting prompts do NOT constitute failure.

keyboardShortcuts.Ctrl+Z: Undo (for cleanup after typing test text)
keyboardShortcuts.Ctrl+Shift+Esc: Open Task Manager (for force-closing frozen apps)
